title: IHL Group homepage: retail technology research and advisory
answer: This is the homepage of IHL Group, a retail technology research and advisory firm. It is a landing page that lists IHL studies, article summaries and vendor case studies from 2026. Its most useful single point is from a September 10, 2026 study of 96 specialty retail brands, in cooperation with Chain Store Age, which finds that inventory data accuracy, not AI budget size, separates specialty retail winners from laggards. The page also states that most retail AI budgets fund the wrong layer first.

sections.body: IHL Group publishes this page. It is the company's homepage and a landing page for its retail technology research and advisory services. The supplied text is dated by its items, with study and article summaries from August 6, August 26 and September 10, 2026, and it was harvested on September 27, 2026. Its scope is retail technology and AI, including inventory visibility, AI budgets, pricing, store digital twins, delivery visibility and some non-retail life sciences work. It is not a single report but a collection of headlines, short summaries and links.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: IHL Group says it offers detailed research and advisory services for retail technology. The page highlights an OnDemand report, SPEND SMART: How Smart Technology and AI Are Closing the Inventory Visibility Gap in Specialty Stores, by Greg Buzek. A September 10, 2026 item says IHL's 2026 study of 96 specialty retail brands, in cooperation with Chain Store Age, finds inventory data accuracy, not AI budget size, separates specialty retail winners from laggards. An August 26, 2026 item says most retail AI budgets fund the wrong layer first, and it points to what is stalling AI pilots before they reach the store floor. An August 6, 2026 item says inventory distortion is down to $1.7 trillion, but empty shelves still cost $690.9 billion, and AI agents no longer wait. GE Appliances is deploying autonomous vehicles, robotics, AI cameras and sensors, and its Brilliant Factory data platform at its Roper Corp. plant in Georgia, with tools that detect defects, predict equipment failures, optimize staffing and forecast demand. Nature's Emporium has partnered with Retailgrid to strengthen pricing decisions across Ontario organic and natural-goods stores, using an AI-powered spreadsheet and Price Radar to integrate daily sales data, model demand and price elasticity, and track four key natural-products competitors plus Amazon.ca. Rainbow has opened an upgraded Shahe sp@ce supermarket in Shenzhen, its first Store Digital Twin site, built with Hanshow and Lingzhi Digital Technology, using 17,000 IoT devices, NexConnect Smart Carts, Nebular Ultra ESLs, AI vision, robotics and retail AI.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: IHL Group's page states that its September 10, 2026 study covers 96 specialty retail brands and finds inventory data accuracy, not AI budget size, separates specialty retail winners from laggards. It states that an August 26, 2026 item finds most retail AI budgets fund the wrong layer first. It states that an August 6, 2026 item puts inventory distortion at $1.7 trillion, with empty shelves still costing $690.9 billion. It states that Nature's Emporium's Retailgrid work tracks four key natural-products competitors plus Amazon.ca. It states that Rainbow's Shahe sp@ce supermarket uses 17,000 IoT devices. It states that Claritas Rx improved fill rates 20% and refill rates 17%. It states that Dr. Squatch achieved a 31.89% recommendation click-through rate, attributed $32,978 in Q1 revenue, cut WISMO inquiries 25%, and reached 94% delivery-date accuracy.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in retail can use this page as a quick pointer to IHL Group's current positions on retail AI spending and inventory visibility, and to case summaries that show AI applied to pricing, store operations, delivery and manufacturing. The most relevant claim is that inventory data accuracy, not AI budget size, separates specialty retail winners from laggards, which challenges a simple spend-more approach. The page also signals that IHL sees many AI budgets funding the wrong layer first. Because it is a landing page, it is best used to identify reports, replays and slides to pursue, not as a standalone evidence base.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Retail

sections.body: This is a commercial research and advisory firm's homepage, not a full report. The supplied text gives short summaries, headlines and links, with no methodology, sample design beyond the 96 specialty retail brands, or independent verification. It mixes IHL studies with vendor case studies and an award item. It is dated by its 2026 items and was harvested on September 27, 2026. The supplied text does not mention grocery, apparel or general merchandise coverage, and it does not give a software spend figure, so it cannot support those specific claims on its own.
